full_judgment:
3. Short facts for the disposal of these Rules are that Mr. Tayeb as pre-emptor filed Miscellaneous Case No. 53 of 1987 on 16-11-87 for pre-emption under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act against Haji Nazir Ahmed as pre-emptee-opposite party No. 1 and others stating, inter alia that he is a co-sharer in the disputed Jama along with opposite party Nos. 2 and 2ka therein and others; the opposition party Nos. 2 and 2ka sold the case land described in the schedule to the petition in favour of one Haji Najir Ahmed by virture of two kabalas dated 16-11-84 and 2-3-87 respectively beyond the knowledge of the pre-emptor. The first kabala dated 16-11-82 (Exhibit 8), registered on 9-12-84 is in respect of 30-2/3 decimals of land and the second one dated 3-3-87 registered on 10-8-87 is in respect of 91 decimals of land out of which the pre-emptor claimed pre-emption for 61-1/3 decimals of land (Exhibit 8 ka), And the pre-emptor came to know about the impugned Kabalas on 1-10-87 corresponding to 14th Aswin, 1394 BS from Abdul Jabbar the bargadar of the case land. The purchaser of the case land Haji Nazir Ahmed was not a co-sharer in the holding, he was an absolute stranger to the case land. 

 4. Subsequently, in the said Miscellaneous Case, Salema Khatun, the wife of opposite party No. 1 Haji Nazir Ahmed was added as opposite party No. 85. The opposite party No. 1 and the added opposite party No. 85 contested the said Misc. Case by filing two separate written statements asserting more or less the same thing, denied the material allegations contending further that the Misc. Case was barred by limitation. The opposite party No. 1 purchased the case land within the knowledge of the pre-emptor and other co-sharers of the case holding, got his name mutated in the relevant record of rights and thereafter gifted the entire case land in favour of his wife Salema Khatun by two registered deeds of gift dated 7-2-87 and 22-8-87 and made over the possession to her. 

 9. Having placed Section 96(1) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act Mr. SC Das submits that as per sub-section (10)(c) of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, the pre-emption case against opposite party No. 85 is not maintainable as she has acquired the case land from her husband, by way of gift. 

 Section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act reads as follows: 

 (a) a transfer to a co-sharer in the tenancy whose interest has accrued otherwise than by purchase; or 

 13. I have already noticed that sub-section (10) of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act has no application under the facts and circumstances of the present case. I am also of the view that the decision reported in 35 DLR 238 is applicable to the present case. 

 17. For the reasons, stated above, I find no ground for interference in these Rules.
